themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Anthropic set its IPO terms: 825 million shares at $70 to $78, up to $64.4 billion, plus a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price from Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC, for up to $90.4 billion in all. The top of the range values it near $1.02 trillion, down from talk of $1.5 trillion; Q3 revenue was $16.96 billion, up 47% from Q2, and compute commitments are nearly $900 billion (Reuters, Nov 10). It will list on Nasdaq as ANT; no pricing date was given.
themes.for_you: No action. The chip and cloud makers are buying into their own customer, which ties about $900 billion of compute orders to a public stock. MSFT and NVDA are left out of the lists: a deal this size can also pull money out of other AI shares in the weeks it trades. None of these names has a buy verdict; AVGO and AMD are on watch only.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: Hims and Hers Q3: revenue $890.4 million, up 49%, but subscribers fell about 100,000 from Q2 to 2.788 million, gross margin dropped to 57% from 74%, and it cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $257 million to $277 million, the third cut this year (company 8-K, Nov 9; StockTitan). HIMS fell 11.8% to 22.94 on Nov 9 before the report (Massive) and traded near 22.22 after hours.
themes.for_you: No action. HIMS moved from 'Accumulate on pullback' to 'Wait' and sits under its 26.32 to 29.16 zone. Cash pay GLP-1 growth now costs margin. No put.

themes.name: Robotics, Automation and Physical AI
themes.what: Rockwell Automation's CEO filed a Form 4 on Nov 9 (EDGAR). The dashboard reads it as an open market buy of about $1.55 million at $386.36 on Nov 9, raising his stake about 4%; his last open market buy found was in February 2024. ROK closed 389.36 on Nov 9 on 1.44 million shares (Massive).
themes.for_you: Watch only. A CEO buying with his own money is the strongest kind of insider signal, but ROK is rated 'Wait', is down 10% in a month and lags SPY over 3 months. Not a swing or put today.

themes.name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
themes.what: Rocket Lab posted record Q3 revenue of $267.8 million, up 73%, and a $3.57 billion backlog, up 52% from Q2, but Neutron's first launch is now no earlier than 2027 and Q4 guidance is $270 million to $290 million (company 8-K, Nov 9). AST SpaceMobile reported Q3 revenue of $42.3 million and pushed its target of about 45 satellites in orbit to mid 2027 from end of 2026 (company 8-K, Nov 9). RKLB traded near 53.30 on Nov 10, down 9.5% from the 58.86 close (Yahoo).
themes.for_you: No action. RKLB is rated Avoid and ASTS has no usable verdict. Orders are growing, but both pushed their key dates out; no swing or put.

innovations.name: Communications
innovations.what: AST SpaceMobile now targets about 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid 2027, not end of 2026; Q3 revenue was $42.3 million, and launch deals cover more than 100 satellites for 2027 and 2028 (AST 8-K, Nov 9). No stage move: the network is still being built.
innovations.for_you: No action. ASTS (36.89 on Nov 9, Massive) has no usable verdict; a six month slip in coverage pushes out revenue.

innovations.name: Defense and Security
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. After the Nov 3 midterms, industry and government officials told Ars Technica they expect the new Democratic majority to set limits on Golden Dome funding and possibly strip out boost phase space based interceptors, the costliest part; two of its top backers in Congress are leaving (KeepTrack citing Ars Technica, Nov 10). The other four innovations had no new hard evidence: the HACM first flight (Oct 5) and LOCUST X3 timing are already logged. No stage moves.
innovations.for_you: LMT is 'Buy zone now' (588.19 on Nov 9, a bit above its 532.15 to 581.10 zone); its case rests on missiles and jets, not on space interceptors, so this does not change the verdict. RTX is 'Accumulate on pullback'. No new buys from this.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Brent fell below $90 a barrel on Nov 10 for the first time since August (Reuters); it was $90.23 at 5:33am ET with a low of $89.21 (Hawksmoor citing market data), and WTI traded near $84.20, down about 3%, after CPI (Yahoo). Fed Governor Waller said Hormuz insurance and ship to ship transfers still add $20 to $30 a barrel.
countries.for_you: No energy setups and no energy puts. DAL (91.80 on Nov 9) is 'Accumulate on pullback' and above its zone; cheaper fuel helps it but there is still nothing to buy.
